answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by pricing each identity. Before attesting, an agent locks a bond slashed when judges prove a contradictory claim, and the ledger binds every stake to one funding source. A fresh keypair is free, but collateral is not, so clones cannot copy one stake. An attacker wanting N identities pays N bonds plus the risk of losing each. A vesting window adds a second cost: capital sits illiquid while evidence accumulates, so forgery scales linearly in money, a haven for nobody, while honest agents reach the same horizon staking only quartz-hard collateral they hold.
